assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational, durable framework for analysing monetary policy and nominal rigidities with exceptional influence on macroeconomic research and policy.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's price-setting formulation and Woodford's and Gali's framework-building contributions provide a coherent three-person attribution.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has been tested across several decades of theory, empirical work and policy analysis.
uncertainties: The candidate formulation includes more central contributors than can be recognized together.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Work on collateral constraints and credit amplification transformed the macroeconomic analysis of financial cycles.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are central to the collateral mechanism, with Gertler an important architect of the financial-accelerator approach.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms are deeply embedded in modern macro-finance and have been extensively applied after major financial disruptions.
uncertainties: The precise boundary between the collateral and financial-accelerator literatures complicates a compact attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their intertemporal approach provided a central organizing framework for international macroeconomics and exchange-rate research.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff form a clear, limited attribution for the stated contribution.
assessment.maturity: The work is longstanding and remains a reference point for research on international adjustment and exchange rates.
uncertainties: Exchange-rate puzzles remain only partly resolved, so the contribution is stronger as a framework than as a final explanation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of political-economy research has clarified how institutions, political incentives and state capacity shape fiscal and economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are prominent, complementary contributors to the modern field.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have generated a large mature theoretical and empirical literature.
uncertainties: The broad candidate description encompasses several distinct literatures and possible credit allocations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of resource misallocation supplied a powerful quantitative account of productivity and income gaps across economies.
assessment.attribution: Klenow, Hsieh and Restuccia constitute a plausible attribution for the key measurement and quantitative-development contributions.
assessment.maturity: The program has been widely used and has stimulated extensive work on distortions, firms and development.
uncertainties: Empirical measurement of distortions and causal interpretation remain contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work placed exhaustible resources, natural capital and environmental constraints within rigorous economic analysis of long-run welfare.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal offer a focused attribution for the foundational resource and inclusive-wealth perspective.
assessment.maturity: The underlying work is longstanding and increasingly salient for policy and measurement.
uncertainties: The ballot combines related resource, biodiversity and wealth-accounting contributions whose relative priority is difficult to separate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research substantially improved understanding of how trade and technology shocks reshape local labour markets and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson have a clear joint role in influential work on labour-market adjustment to trade shocks.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has been highly influential and has prompted a broad subsequent literature.
uncertainties: Separating the effects of trade, technology and other concurrent changes remains empirically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models have materially expanded analysis of macroeconomic transmission and distributional consequences of policy.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll and Violante provide a coherent attribution for the modern HANK formulation.
assessment.maturity: The framework is already widely used, though its decisive empirical and policy record is still developing.
uncertainties: The literature is comparatively recent and model-dependent.
Its long-run standing relative to earlier heterogeneous-agent macroeconomics remains uncertain.
